raw.assessment: The incumbent accommodates telephone and desk requests and gave eleven groups a weekly booking, supporting partial access. It does not establish the eight-week target: needs and acceptable windows are unknown, three access conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly. A concrete limit on interpreting 68% reservation coverage as usable spare capacity is the sole acoustic piano: seven bookings required it and remaining equipment fields were blank. Together with evening request concentration, this leaves both resource-specific scarcity and avoidable allocation mismatch plausible. Late or missed sessions do not establish that their time could have served another group.

openings.claim: Some rejected requests may reflect inherited timing and unrecorded room compatibility rather than unavoidable shortage within the existing staffed hours.
openings.delta: Assess feasible rehearsal assignments using stated needs, acceptable windows and essential equipment instead of aggregate reservation coverage.
openings.prediction: If mismatch matters, at least one rejected need can fit through a mutually accepted reassignment while preserving every requesting group's weekly 60-minute access and both performances. If all feasible alternatives fail on timing or piano availability, scarcity gains support.
openings.probe: Use short telephone or desk conversations to record weekly needs, acceptable windows and essential equipment for all twelve groups. Construct one proposed weekly allocation within existing hours, verify acceptance before changes, and count fulfilled needs and volunteer minutes. Treat an infeasible allocation as a finding, not permission to relax guarantees.
assumptions: Some inherited reservations may be voluntarily reassigned; this is unverified.

openings.claim: Ambiguous or inconsistently propagated changes may contribute to access conflicts and administrative effort; only one conflict is explicitly tied to calendar disagreement.
openings.delta: Test whether a single authoritative reservation record plus verbal confirmation prevents divergent expectations across existing channels.
openings.prediction: If change propagation is causal, disputed arrivals will trace to stale or unacknowledged changes; conflicts persisting despite matching records and confirmations would weaken this account.
openings.probe: For a bounded trial, assign booking identifiers in the paper master, read back room, date and time for every change, and mark when the online copy is updated. At disputed arrivals compare expectations with the change record. Include confirmation and copying time in weekly administration totals.
assumptions: The volunteer and desk can consistently consult the master.
Any conflict reduction must outweigh added recordkeeping to meet the administration target.

raw.assessment: Missing acceptable windows and equipment requirements prevent a capacity diagnosis. The observations justify testing interactions, but establish neither their benefit nor eight-week feasibility.

openings.claim: Combine a weekly 60-minute entitlement pass with matching against stated time windows and equipment needs. At the group-to-slot eligibility interface, allocate compatible minimum slots before supplemental rehearsal time; explicitly verify blank equipment entries.
openings.delta: An entitlement pass alone can consume scarce piano or evening capacity unnecessarily; compatibility matching alone can favor groups receiving longer bookings. Their combination could protect minimum access while satisfying more stated needs.
openings.prediction: With identical demand, the combined allocation will meet more requested minutes within acceptable windows than either component alone while retaining every requested weekly minimum. No advantage is expected if all unmet demand requires the same saturated slots.
openings.probe: Collect upcoming needs through short calls or desk conversations. Compare incumbent, entitlement-only, matching-only and combined schedules using identical room-hours and protected performances. Check equipment compatibility, group minimums and scheduling effort before any changes; measure actual fulfillment during the eight weeks.
assumptions: Feasible schedules exist within staffed hours.
Needs collection and allocation can fit the administration budget.

openings.claim: Combine mutually agreed reservation swaps with a single authoritative desk ledger. At the swap-commit interface, hold both original bookings until both contacts agree, then record both replacements together and confirm them by telephone or in person; derive the online display from that ledger.
openings.delta: Swaps could improve compatibility but introduce conflicting expectations; ledger consistency alone cannot improve unsuitable assignments. One confirmed exchange could supply both improvements.
openings.prediction: Where reciprocal compatible alternatives exist, confirmed swaps will improve fulfillment without duplicate active reservations; unconfirmed exchanges will leave original access intact.
openings.probe: Test one volunteered exchange, preserving equipment compatibility, weekly minimums and performances. Log contact time, ledger/display agreement, each group's understanding and actual attendance. Compare with a direct change of similar complexity.
assumptions: Staff consistently consult the authoritative ledger.
Confirmation overhead remains within two administration hours weekly.

openings.claim: Inherited timing and unknown compatibility may cause rejection. Allocate compatible weekly minima before supplemental time to combine access protection with matching.
openings.discriminator: Accepted reassignment supports mismatch; saturated acceptable piano/evening slots support scarcity. Compare incumbent, entitlement-only, matching-only and combined allocations.
openings.fit: Preserves C1-C4; infeasibility cannot relax guarantees.
openings.probe: Call or interview twelve contacts for needs, windows and equipment, including blanks. Compare identical-demand schedules, obtain acceptance, and measure fulfillment and effort.
openings.uncertainty: Contacts' representativeness, flexibility, feasibility and administrative cost remain unknown.

openings.claim: Stale or unacknowledged changes may cause conflicts; a paper master with identifiers and verbal readback could align expectations.
openings.discriminator: Trace disputed arrivals to changes; conflicts despite aligned records weaken this account.
openings.probe: Trial booking identifiers, room/date/time readback and online-update marks; compare disputed expectations and count all copying/confirmation time.
openings.uncertainty: Only one conflict explicitly involved calendar disagreement; consistent master use and net time savings are unverified.

openings.claim: Agreed reciprocal swaps plus atomic ledger updates may improve compatibility without duplicate expectations; retain originals until both contacts agree.
openings.discriminator: Compatible confirmed swaps improve fulfillment; unconfirmed swaps preserve original access.
openings.fit: Preserves C1-C4, equipment compatibility and minima.
openings.probe: Trial one volunteered exchange; commit both replacements together, confirm through existing channels, update display, and compare understanding, attendance and contact effort with a similar direct change.
openings.uncertainty: Reciprocal alternatives, ledger adherence and affordable confirmation overhead are unverified.

post_distill.decision: Collect needs first. Preserve two rooms, existing hours/equipment, no fees, performances and requested weekly 60-minute access. Reserved capacity and lateness do not prove recoverable time. Eight-week success remains unestablished: measure 90% needs fulfillment, fewer than two conflicts and administration averaging at most two hours weekly.
